evals.prompt: Read the attached design spec once, start to finish, at normal reading pace (no re-reading, no external tools). Then, from memory of what you just read, reconstruct the full webhook delivery state machine: list every state, every transition (source state -> target state, with its trigger/condition), and which states are terminal.
evals.expected_output: A complete and accurate state transition table for the webhook delivery retry lifecycle, matching the spec exactly.
expectations: Lists all 6 states: pending, delivering, delivered, retrying, dead_letter, cancelled
Correctly identifies all 3 terminal states: delivered, dead_letter, cancelled
Correctly states the retry cap is 5 attempts before moving to dead_letter
Correctly identifies that cancellation is reachable from all three non-terminal states (pending, delivering, retrying) — not just from one
Correctly identifies the retry loop (retrying -> delivering after backoff elapses) as a cycle that can repeat, not a single one-way transition
No hallucinated state or transition (e.g. no delivering -> pending, no invented states like 'paused' or 'queued')
